{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=computational+discovery+problem+formulation+metrics+for+autonomous+agents&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.20944/preprints202603.1694.v1\", \"title\": [\"A Brief History of AI for Scientific Discovery: Open Research, Metrics, and Autonomous Agents\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The history of artificial intelligence for scientific discovery is not a two year story about chatbots learning to write papers. It is a sixty year story about science repeatedly handing its bottlenecks to machines—first inference, then search, then measurement, then the full workflow—only to discover that each delegation solves one problem and exposes a harder one underneath. This paper traces that history from DENDRAL (1965) through the construction of open scholarly infrastructure (arXiv, Google Scholar, ORCID), the oracle breakthroughs of AlphaFold, and the current era of LLM driven autonomous research agents. Three interlocking threads are followed including AI as research instrument, AI for research infrastructure, and the reshaping of scholarly profiles and incentives by machine readable metrics. The central tension throughout is between automation and augmentation between building systems that replace human researchers and tools that amplify human creativity and judgement. The paper presents that the most consequential development is not any single tool but the emergence of an interconnected ecosystem where AI agents, preprint platforms, open source codebases, and citation infrastructure form a feedback loop that is fundamentally restructuring who can do science, how fast discoveries propagate, and what counts as a valid scientific contribution.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202603.1694.v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 3, 23]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.65109/dwjt8467\", \"title\": [\"Basis function discovery using spectral clustering and bisimulation metrics\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) are a powerful framework for modeling sequential decision making for intelligent agents acting in stochastic environments. One of the important challenges facing such agents in practical applications is finding a suitable way to represent the state space, so that a good way of behaving can be learned efficiently. In this paper, we focus on learning a good policy when function approximation must be used to represent the value function. In this case, states are mapped into feature vectors, and a set of parameters is learned, which allows us to approximate the value of any given state. Theoretically, the quality of the approximation that can be obtained depends on the set of features. In practice, the feature set affects not only the quality of the solution obtained, but also the speed of learning.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.65109/dwjt8467\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2011, 5, 2]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.7717/peerj-cs.3756/table-11\", \"title\": [\"Table 11: Metrics and their relationship with domains in autonomous agents.\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj-cs.3756/table-11\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1021/acs.chemmater.2c03118.s001\", \"title\": [\"The Autonomous Formulation Laboratory: An Open Liquid Handling Platform for Formulation Discovery Using Xray and Neutron Scattering\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.chemmater.2c03118.s001\"}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "44becccf85c73501976fa588454322582832be4b934a22a2f21d3825fba3ec77", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unassigned_problem", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.20944/preprints202603.1694.v1", "doi:10.65109/dwjt8467", "doi:10.7717/peerj-cs.3756/table-11", "doi:10.1021/acs.chemmater.2c03118.s001"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202603.1694.v1", "https://doi.org/10.65109/dwjt8467", "https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj-cs.3756/table-11", "https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.chemmater.2c03118.s001"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
